# Feature: Run Results & Audit

## 1. Feature Goal

**ID**: FEAT-066
**Source Plan**: `.spec-lite/plan_ui.md`

Every run Yantra has ever recorded gets a complete, trustworthy page in the Yantra app. The
**Ledger** lists all runs, including runs started from the CLI or the daemon. It pages by cursor,
filters by outcome, mode, date and text, and picks up new runs without a reload. Each run opens a
**Run result** (`/runs/<id>`).

- **When a Brief or templated document exists**, the page renders it: overview, findings,
  sections, condition statuses, cited rows, Sources and Also consulted, captures and notices.
- **When none exists**, the page shows outputs, the terminal reason, run health, `report.md` and
  artifacts.

Every source citation `[n]` and action citation `A<n>` opens its evidence in one click. Runs with
no recorded evidence say so explicitly. **Audit** renders the same story as `yantra audit`.

The app serves only artifacts that a public allowlist names, through bounded viewers. Corrupt,
missing, legacy and very large artifacts fail per item, never per page. A run with 50,000 events
stays responsive.

This is the M1 read-only slice (plan §8 Delivery milestones). It is the first app surface with real
value, and it closes the TODO "Web UI for browsing/sharing Briefs" (plan §16).

**Business value:** a user who does not use a terminal can review what any run did, check every
claim against its evidence, and audit secret use, consent and model calls. All of it follows the
CLI's words exactly (memory → General: CLI ↔ app parity).

> **Plan notes (no deviation):**
>
> - **The `[n]` quote.** A Brief persists one `excerpt` per source (`BriefSource.excerpt`), not a
>   quote per claim. The EvidencePane therefore shows the source's recorded excerpt as "its quote",
>   and says "Quote not recorded for this run" when `excerpt` is `null`. Claim-level quote spans are
>   logged in `TODO.md` (see §6).
> - **The run-result read.** `read.run_result` belongs to the `open` command's app adapter. The plan
>   §6 execution-class table lists `open` as "adapter: in-app result view", and D16 allows explicit
>   adapters. All other reads used here are the `read.<name>` reads of the `list`, `audit` and
>   `report` read-class commands.
> - **Pagination beyond CLI flags.** Ledger filters (outcome, mode, date, text) and cursors are RPC
>   parameters of `read.list`. The plan §6 allows "cursor pagination where lists can grow", and
>   FEAT-066 scope names those filters. Adding matching `yantra list` flags is out of scope and
>   tracked in `TODO.md`.

## 2. Data Model (Granular)

> `.spec-lite/data_model.md` does not exist. This feature adds **no new tables**. It adds one index
> migration to the existing `history` table and a set of Zod schemas in `@yantra/protocol`, which
> are the wire contract between the host and `apps/web` (the web app imports protocol types only,
> plan §8). Every on-disk run artifact keeps its shape (plan §6 "Unchanged files").

### Entities & Attributes

**Protocol: run identity and artifact registry** (`packages/protocol/src/schemas/run-artifacts.ts`)

- **`RunId`** (string): `^[0-9]{8}T[0-9]{6}Z-[A-Za-z0-9-]+$`, at most 96 characters. It accepts
  every id `formatRunId` produces and rejects separators, `..` and drive letters. Every read that
  takes a run id validates it before touching the filesystem.
- **`RunArtifactExposure`** (enum): `typed | view | download | denied`.
  - `typed`: reaches the app only through a typed read, such as `brief.json` through
    `read.run_result`.
  - `view`: readable through a bounded viewer.
  - `download`: served only as an attachment.
  - `denied`: never served.
- **`RunArtifactViewer`** (enum): `brief | document | markdown | json | jsonl | text | image | none`.
- **`RunArtifactRegistryEntry`**:
  - `id` (string, UNIQUE): stable entry name, for example `brief.json` or `screenshots`.
  - `pattern` (string): the run-relative, forward-slash glob the entry matches. Examples:
    `brief.json`, `agent/*.jsonl`, `screenshots/*.png`, `captures/cap-*.txt`.
  - `exposure` (`RunArtifactExposure`).
  - `viewer` (`RunArtifactViewer`).
  - `media_type` (string): the only `Content-Type` the host may send for the entry. HTML entries
    are `text/html` with `download` exposure only.
  - `inline_cap_bytes` (int | null): the largest file a viewer may load whole. Above it, the item
    becomes `too_large` and offers "Show in folder" or download.
  - `description` (string): Zod `.describe` text for the generated docs and the FEAT-070 parity
    test.
- **`RUN_ARTIFACT_REGISTRY`** (readonly array): the **public allowlist**. Matching is
  first-match-wins, explicit denials come first, and **anything unmatched is `denied`**.
  - **Explicit denials:** `lease.json`, `reconcile.lock`, `.lock`, `decisions/**`, `*.tmp`,
    `**/*.tmp`, sockets, `**/chrome-profile/**`, and any browser-profile directory.
  - **Allowed entries** (each is `view` unless noted; size caps in parentheses):
    - `brief.json`: `typed`, viewer `brief`, 512 KiB.
    - `brief.md`: viewer `markdown`, 2 MiB.
    - `brief.html`: `download` only.
    - `document.json`: `typed`, viewer `document`, 512 KiB.
    - `document.md`: viewer `markdown`.
    - `document.html`: `download` only.
    - `report.md`: viewer `markdown`, 512 KiB.
    - `outputs.json`, `manifest.json`, `usage.json`, `run-health.json`, `contract.json`,
      `trace.json`, `schedule.json` and `execution-receipt.json` (FEAT-072; non-secret by
      construction): viewer `json`, 2 MiB.
    - `events.jsonl`, `run-events.jsonl`, `runtime.jsonl`, `tool-calls.jsonl`,
      `confirmations.jsonl`, `secrets.jsonl` (key names only), `interventions.jsonl`,
      `agent.jsonl` (legacy) and `agent/*.jsonl` (the provider session log): viewer `jsonl`,
      windowed with no whole-file cap.
    - `screenshots/*.png`, which must also match `SCREENSHOT_ARTIFACT_PATH_PATTERN`: viewer
      `image`, 20 MiB.
    - `captures/cap-*.txt`: viewer `text`, 2 MiB.
    - `captures/*.png`: viewer `image`, 20 MiB.
- **`classifyRunArtifact(relPath)`**: a pure function returning the matching entry or the denial
  entry. Paths are normalized to forward slashes first. Absolute paths, `..`, backslashes and NUL
  are always `denied`.

**Protocol: CLI `--json` read schemas** (`packages/protocol/src/schemas/cli-reads.ts`). These close
the `read`-class schema gap in `TODO.md` for `list`, `audit` and `report`.

- **`ListRunItem`**. It matches today's `list --json` run item exactly:
  - `kind: 'run'`;
  - `runId`;
  - `workflowName`;
  - `status` (string: the history status or the manifest status, exactly as the CLI prints it);
  - `startedAt`;
  - `durationMs` (number | null);
  - `taskOutcome?` (`TaskOutcome`).

  It adds these **optional, additive** fields, emitted by both the CLI and the host:
  - `taskType?` (`ask | research | do | run`);
  - `executionState?` (`interrupted`, from FEAT-064 when present);
  - `costUsd?` (number | null);
  - `hasDocument?` (boolean).

- **`ListWorkflowItem`**: the existing workflow item, unchanged.
- **`ListResult`**: `{schemaVersion, kind: 'list', items}`.
- **`RunLedgerQuery`** (RPC params of `read.list` for target `runs`):
  - `cursor?` (opaque string);
  - `limit` (int, 1–200, default 50);
  - `outcome?` (`TaskOutcome[]`, plus `unknown` for legacy rows without one);
  - `mode?` (`TaskType[]`);
  - `since?` and `until?` (ISO-8601);
  - `text?` (1–200 characters; a case-insensitive substring of the intent text or run id);
  - `workflow?` and `status?` (the existing CLI filters, same semantics).
- **`RunLedgerPage`**: `ListResult` plus:
  - `next_cursor` (string | null);
  - `source` (`index | files`);
  - `scan_truncated` (boolean, only on the file fallback);
  - `active` (an array of `ListRunItem` plus `displayedState`, see TASK-003).
- **`LedgerCursor`** (internal and versioned): base64url JSON
  `{v: 1, started_at, run_id, source}`. A cursor that is not base64url or fails the schema is a
  validation error (RPC invalid params). It never falls back to page one.
- **`AuditReport`**. The Zod form of today's `AuditRenderReport` (`apps/cli/src/render/types.ts`),
  field for field: runId, workflowName, status, startedAt, endedAt, durationMs, llmCallCount,
  secretLookups, stepCount, scopeMix, trustNarrative, agent, toolCalls, captures,
  rawSessionLogCaptureBearing, usage, terminalError. `AuditRenderReport` becomes
  `z.infer<typeof AuditReport>`. `audit --json` output stays **byte-identical**.
- **`AuditPage`** (RPC result of `read.audit`): `{report: AuditReport, tool_calls: {total,
next_cursor}, captures: {total, next_cursor}}`. In it, `report.toolCalls` and `report.captures`
  hold only the requested window (at most 500 rows each), so a 50,000-call run never exceeds the
  WebSocket message limit.
- **`ReportResult`**: `{schemaVersion, kind: 'report', markdown}`, today's `report --json`. The host
  read adds `truncated: boolean` and `bytes: number` when `report.md` exceeds its cap.

**Protocol: run-result view** (`packages/protocol/src/schemas/run-result.ts`)

- **`ArtifactSlot<T>`** (discriminated union on `state`):
  - `{state: 'ok', value: T, path}`;
  - `{state: 'missing', path}`;
  - `{state: 'corrupt', path, detail}`. `detail` is a bounded (≤200 characters) parse or Zod
    summary, never file content.
  - `{state: 'unsupported', path, found_version}`. For example, a Brief whose `schema_version` is
    not `0.2`.
  - `{state: 'too_large', path, bytes, cap}`.
  - `{state: 'denied', path}` (defensive; never expected for registry paths).
- **`RunResultView`** (RPC result of `read.run_result`; at most 768 KiB serialized):
  - `run_id` (`RunId`).
  - `mode` (`ask | research | do | run | unknown`).
  - `title` (string): the Brief or document title, else the intent text or query, else the workflow
    name.
  - `started_at`, `ended_at` (ISO | null) and `duration_ms` (int | null).
  - `status` (string): the manifest status as the CLI prints it.
  - `task_outcome` (`TaskOutcome` | null).
  - `termination_reason` (`TerminationReason` | null).
  - `execution_state` (`interrupted` | null, from FEAT-064).
  - `live` (`{state: 'running' | 'waiting_for_you' | 'unknown_owner'} | null`): present only while
    a lease exists (FEAT-064). `unknown_owner` covers a manifest that says running but whose owner
    cannot be verified (memory → Architecture: `unknown` is never treated as dead).
  - `document`: `{kind: 'brief', slot: ArtifactSlot<Brief>}`, or
    `{kind: 'templated_report', slot: ArtifactSlot<TemplatedReport>}`, or `{kind: 'none'}`.
  - `outputs` (`ArtifactSlot<Record<string, unknown>>`): only for workflow runs, capped at 256 KiB.
  - `terminal` (`TerminalReason` | null): `{source: 'run_outcome' | 'manifest' | 'events' |
'report', failure_class?, message?, blocker?, safest_next_action?, termination_reason?}`. All
    text is bounded to 500 characters and stripped of ANSI.
  - `run_health` (`ArtifactSlot<RunHealth>`).
  - `report` (`{exists: boolean, bytes: number | null}`): the body is fetched lazily through
    `read.report`.
  - `artifacts` (`ArtifactInventoryItem[]`, at most 2,000, with an `artifacts_truncated` flag).
  - `notices_source` (`brief | document | run_health | none`): tells the UI where the Notices
    block comes from.
- **`ArtifactInventoryItem`**: `{path, entry_id, exposure, viewer, bytes, modified_at,
over_inline_cap: boolean}`. Denied files are **omitted entirely**, so the inventory never names
  them.
- **`JsonlWindowRequest`**: `{run_id, path, from_line (int ≥ 0), limit (1–200)}`.
- **`JsonlWindow`**: `{path, total_lines_known, total_complete: boolean, from_line, lines:
{n, text, truncated_bytes}[], partial_tail: boolean}`.
  - Each line's text is capped at 16 KiB. `truncated_bytes` reports how much was cut.
  - A window is at most 512 KiB.
  - A trailing partial line is reported through `partial_tail` and never returned (plan §8 tail
    recovery).

**Web-side state** (`apps/web`, no persistence beyond URL state):

- **`LedgerFilters`**: outcome, mode, since, until and text, mirrored in the route's search params,
  so a filtered view is a shareable in-app URL.
- **Query keys**: `['ledger', filters]` (infinite), `['run', runId]`, `['audit', runId, window]`,
  `['report', runId]`, `['jsonl', runId, path, fromLine]`.

### Relationships

- `history.run_id` 1:1 with the run directory `runs/<run_id>/` (existing).
- `RunResultView` 1:1 with a run directory. Its `document`, `outputs`, `run_health` and `artifacts`
  each map to one or more files in that directory through `RUN_ARTIFACT_REGISTRY`.
- `Brief.key_findings[].citations[]`, `sections[].citations[]`, `constraints[].citations[]` and
  `facets.comparison.row_citations[][]` each resolve N:1 to `Brief.sources[].n`, guaranteed by the
  existing schema refinement.
- `Brief.key_findings[].actions[]`, `sections[].actions[]` and `facets.comparison.row_actions[][]`
  each resolve N:1 to `Brief.actions[].id` (`A<n>`).
- A `BriefAction.artifacts[]` entry (`ArtifactRef`) resolves 1:1 to a `screenshots/*.png` registry
  entry, served through a signed URL.

### Indexes & Constraints

- **Migration (next free `index.db` version; v5 at the time of writing):** `CREATE INDEX
idx_history_started_run ON history(started_at DESC, run_id DESC)` supports keyset paging on
  `(started_at, run_id)`. It is additive and idempotent under `runMigrations`. If another feature
  has already claimed v5, take the next number. Migrations are append-only.
- **Keyset rule:** `WHERE (started_at < ?) OR (started_at = ? AND run_id < ?) ORDER BY started_at
DESC, run_id DESC LIMIT ?`. Ties on `started_at` never skip or duplicate a row.
- **Text filter:** `(intent_text LIKE ? ESCAPE '\\' OR run_id LIKE ? ESCAPE '\\')`, with `%` `_` `\`
  escaped in user input. The query is always parameterized and never concatenated.
- **Outcome filter:** `task_outcome IN (…)`. `unknown` maps to `task_outcome IS NULL`.
- **Response caps:**
  - `RunResultView` ≤ 768 KiB;
  - `AuditPage` ≤ 768 KiB;
  - `JsonlWindow` ≤ 512 KiB.

  All stay under the host's 1 MiB WebSocket message limit (plan §7). A response that would exceed
  its cap degrades the offending slot to `too_large`. It is never truncated mid-JSON.

## 4. Dependencies

- **FEAT-061 (M1 subset), hard.** Tokens, themes and the semantic icon registry. Primitives:
  Button, Link, Table (virtualized, cursor-paged), Tabs, Tooltip, Disclosure, Toast. The gallery
  route and the `axe-core` harness. Raw-color and icon lint.
- **FEAT-062 (read entries), hard.** The registry entries for `list`, `audit`, `report` and `open`.
  The `json.schema` references are filled by TASK-002, TASK-008 and TASK-007 of this feature.
- **FEAT-065 (read-only portion), hard.** Plan §8 Sequencing step 5. It supplies:
  - the host, sessions and per-window capabilities;
  - the `read.<name>` dispatcher;
  - `artifact.url` and `GET /a/<signed>` (this feature supplies the allowlist gate);
  - `runs.subscribe` change hints (lease scan, 2-second history polling, filesystem watch);
  - the `apps/web` skeleton (router, React Query client, app shell);
  - `command.invoke` for "Show in folder".
- **FEAT-064, soft.**
  - **What it supplies:** `executionState: interrupted` (manifest), lease liveness and the reconcile hook.
  - **STUB if it has not landed:** `live` comes from manifest `status: running` alone, shown as
    `unknown_owner`, and the reconcile hook is a no-op. Remove the stub once FEAT-064 lands.
- **FEAT-063, soft.**
  - **What it supplies:** the terminal `run_outcome` event in `run-events.jsonl`.
  - **STUB if it has not landed:** the terminal-reason reader skips the `run_outcome` source, so the
    fallback chain starts at the manifest.
- **FEAT-072, soft.** It supplies `execution-receipt.json`. The registry lists it as `view`, and
  when it is absent the run has no such inventory item.
- **New dependencies, user approval before pinning (memory → Dependencies):** `react-markdown` and
  `remark-gfm` (plan §3), unless an earlier feature already pinned them. No other new dependency;
  virtualization uses React Aria's `Virtualizer` and `ListLayout`, which `react-aria-components`
  already provides.

## 5. Implementation Tasks

### TASK-001: Public-artifact allowlist and a gated artifact path end to end

Only registry-public run files can be signed or served. Everything else, including traversal and
symlink escapes, is unreachable.

- [ ] **Implementation**:
  - **Protocol** `run-artifacts.ts`: `RunId`, the exposure and viewer enums,
    `RunArtifactRegistryEntry` and `RUN_ARTIFACT_REGISTRY` with the entries in §2 (explicit
    denials first, default deny). `classifyRunArtifact(relPath)` normalizes the path and denies
    absolute paths, `..`, `\`, NUL and empty segments. Export it and emit the JSON Schema.
  - **Core** `run-view/artifact-gate.ts`: `resolvePublicArtifact(runsRoot, runId, relPath)`. The
    steps:
    1. validate `RunId`;
    2. classify, and refuse `denied` with `ArtifactAccessError('not_public')`;
    3. resolve the run directory, then `realpath` both it and the target;
    4. require that the target is contained by the run directory (`outside_run`), which defeats
       symlinks and junctions;
    5. `lstat`/`stat` the target, requiring a regular file (`not_found` otherwise);
    6. return `{absPath, entry, bytes, mtime}`.

    `runsRoot` always comes from `paths.ts` (memory → Project Structure).

  - **Host** (FEAT-065 handlers): - `artifact.url {run_id, path}` calls the gate **before** signing. - `GET /a/<signed>` re-runs the gate **at serve time**, because the file may have changed since
    signing. - Responses send `Content-Type: entry.media_type` and `X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff`.
    `download` exposure (including every HTML file) adds `Content-Disposition: attachment;
filename="<basename>"`. - A file over `inline_cap_bytes` is still downloadable when its exposure allows, and it streams
    (never buffered). - Rejections return a uniform 404 with no reason in the body. The host log counts them by
    error code only (plan §11: no signed URLs or tokens).

- [ ] **Unit Tests**:
  - Protocol: a table test classifies every §2 path, including `lease.json`, `decisions/x.json`,
    `brief.json.tmp`, `agent/x.jsonl`, `screenshots/1-abcdef123456.png`, `screenshots/evil.png`
    (fails the grammar, so denied), `../manifest.json`, `a\\b`, `C:/x` and `%2e%2e/x`. Unmatched
    files are denied. Explicit denials beat later allows. Every entry has a description, and
    `media_type` is from the allowlist.
  - Core: traversal is refused. A symlink (POSIX) or junction (Windows) pointing outside the run is
    `outside_run`. A directory is `not_found`. An invalid run id is refused before any filesystem
    call (spy on `realpath`). `runsRoot` resolves through `paths.ts` under a sandboxed
    `YANTRA_HOME` with `resetPathCache()`.
  - Host:
    - signing `lease.json`, `decisions/…` or `../x` is refused;
    - a signed URL for `brief.md` serves with `nosniff` and the registry type;
    - `brief.html` arrives as an attachment;
    - replacing a signed file with a symlink to an outside file between signing and serving gives 404.

      serving in `docs/features/safety-and-privacy.md`: which run files the app can show, which it
      never serves, and that HTML is download-only.

  - `cd packages/core && npx vitest run tests/run-view/artifact-gate.spec.ts`.

One core function pages runs by keyset and filters them. Both `yantra list` and the host's

    - keyset on `(started_at, run_id)`;
    - filters for outcome (`unknown` maps to NULL), mode, since and until, and an escaped `LIKE`
      on the text;
    - fetches `limit + 1` rows to compute `next_cursor`;
    - always parameterized SQL.

null, runStore, activeRuns?: () => Promise<ActiveRun[]>}`: - **Index path:** `HistoryStore.page`. - **File-scan fallback** (index unavailable or rebuilding): list run directory names, sort them
    descending (run ids are lexically start-ordered, per `formatRunId`), apply the keyset on

    index. They come from `activeRuns` (FEAT-065 invocations plus FEAT-064 leases) and, on the
    first page only, from a bounded scan of the newest 200 run directories for `running`
    manifests. Active runs are returned separately in `active` and are never paginated. - **Cursors:** `encodeLedgerCursor` and `decodeLedgerCursor`, versioned and validated. A bad
    cursor throws `LedgerCursorError`.

### TASK-008: Bounded and windowed artifact viewers with "Show in folder" and EventInspector

Any allowlisted artifact opens in a bounded viewer. JSONL of any length is windowed and
virtualized, and files over a cap offer "Show in folder" instead of loading.

- [ ] **Implementation**:
  - **Protocol:** `JsonlWindowRequest` and `JsonlWindow`.
  - **Core** `run-view/jsonl-window.ts`:
    - **`SparseLineIndex`:** streams the file once and records the byte offset every 1,024 lines.
      It is keyed by `(realpath, size, mtimeMs)` in an LRU of 16 files. When a file only grows
      (a live run), the index extends from its last checkpoint instead of rebuilding.
    - **`readJsonlWindow(absPath, from_line, limit, cache)`:** seeks to the nearest checkpoint and
      streams forward.
      - It caps each line at 16 KiB (reporting `truncated_bytes`) and each window at 512 KiB.
      - It never returns a trailing partial line, reporting `partial_tail` instead.
      - `total_complete` is false until the index has reached end of file.
  - **Host `read.artifact_window {run_id, path, from_line, limit}`:** passes through
    `resolvePublicArtifact` (TASK-001) and requires viewer `jsonl`.
  - **Host `artifact.url`** (TASK-001) serves the `json`, `text`, `markdown` and `image` viewers. A
    viewer fetches whole only when `bytes ≤ inline_cap_bytes`.
  - **`apps/web` viewers** (`routes/runs.$runId.artifacts.$.tsx` dispatches by registry viewer):
    - **`JsonlViewer`:** a React Aria `Virtualizer` with `ListLayout`. Fixed-height collapsed rows
      fetch windows of 200 lines on scroll, and a row expands on demand. Each line parses as JSON;
      a parse failure renders the raw text with a "not valid JSON" chip (fails per line).
      `events.jsonl` and `run-events.jsonl` lines that parse as a known `TaskEvent` (or FEAT-063
      `RunEvent`) show a one-line summary. Unknown kinds, or kinds that fail validation, render in
      **EventInspector**.
    - **`JsonViewer`:** a collapsible tree, depth-limited, with strings over 2 KiB collapsed.
    - **`TextViewer`** and **markdown** (SafeMarkdown) for files under the cap.
    - **`ImageViewer`:** a signed URL with natural-size and fit modes.
    - **`ShowInFolder`:** invokes `open <run-id> --artifact dir` through FEAT-065
      `command.invoke`, the plan's `mutate`-worker route for `open`. When invocation is
      unavailable (the read-only host), it shows the copyable CLI twin instead.
  - **`packages/ui` `EventInspector`:** a generic, bounded tree for any JSON object. It shows
    `kind`, `seq` and `ts` first, renders keys and strings escaped, and limits depth to 6 and
    entries to 200 per level ("+N more"). It never interprets content as HTML.

### TASK-010: Run-results evidence suite: resilience, scale, security and parity (M1 end to end)

The plan §10 "Run results (I11 evidence)" and FEAT-066 acceptance items are proven end to end
through a real host and app window.

- [ ] **Implementation**:
  - **`e2e/app-run-results.spec.ts`:** puppeteer-core with the existing Chrome resolution, a
    sandboxed `YANTRA_HOME` and `resetPathCache()`. It starts the FEAT-065 host with
    `LLM_PROVIDER=none` and seeds run directories through the core fixture builders (exported for
    e2e, Vitest-free per memory: `@yantra/test-helpers` must not be imported by `tsx` scripts):
    - every golden Brief;
    - a successful zero-synthesis workflow;
    - a pre-Brief failure;
    - an interrupted legacy run;
    - source and action citations, plus a legacy Brief without `actions`;
    - corrupt `brief.json` and a missing `run-health.json`;
    - a Brief with `schema_version: '0.1'`;
    - a large run (50,000 `events.jsonl` lines, 50,000 `tool-calls.jsonl` entries, and a 300 MB
      capture created with `truncate` so no bytes are written);
    - a run directory containing `lease.json`, `decisions/x.json` and `brief.json.tmp`.
  - **Flows:**
    1. Ledger, then filter, then open a result.
    2. Click every citation chip and assert the pane content.
    3. Open the Audit.
    4. Open `tool-calls.jsonl` and jump to the end.
    5. Attempt `artifact.url` and `GET /a/…` for each denied path, plus traversal variants.
  - **Responsiveness budget** for the large run, on the CI machine profile:
    - `read.run_result` under 300 ms (warm);
    - the first JSONL window under 1 s (cold index), later windows under 150 ms;
    - the Ledger first page under 300 ms;
    - the page never loads the 300 MB capture (assert from network events);
    - long tasks on the app main thread under 200 ms during scroll.

    These run on a stepped measurement with their own test timeout (memory: real-Chrome timeouts).

  - **Parity test:** for each `TaskOutcome` and each status word, the Ledger and result-page text
    equals what `yantra list` prints for the same run directory (run the built CLI against the same
    `YANTRA_HOME`).
  - **Accessibility:** `axe-core` on Ledger, Run result (Brief and no-document), Audit, and each
    viewer, in light and dark. A keyboard-only path goes Ledger, result, chip, pane, back.

## 6. Cross-Cutting Concerns

- **Auth.**
  - Every read (`read.list`, `read.run_result`, `read.audit`, `read.report`,
    `read.artifact_window`) and every `artifact.url` runs only on a WebSocket authenticated with
    the per-window capability (FEAT-065, plan §7).
  - Artifact bytes travel only through signed, path-bound, window-bound URLs that expire after 5
    minutes.
  - This feature adds the allowlist gate on both sides of signing (TASK-001). It introduces no new
    auth mechanism and no CORS headers.
- **Security.**
  - **Default deny:** anything not named by `RUN_ARTIFACT_REGISTRY` is never served or listed.
  - **Path containment:** every path is checked with `realpath` containment inside the run
    directory, which defeats symlinks and Windows junctions.
  - **HTML:** `brief.html` and `document.html` are download-only; the app renders results from JSON
    (§7).
  - **Untrusted text:** titles, excerpts, URLs, model text and JSONL content render through React
    escaping and SafeMarkdown with raw HTML skipped. Markdown images never load. Links are
    `http(s)` only, with `rel="noopener noreferrer"`.
  - **Protected values:** ProtectedValue has no value or length input. Secret lookups show keys
    only.
  - **Canary scope:** the outbound canary scans (FEAT-065 security suite) cover these reads.
    TASK-010 seeds a canary-bearing `secrets.jsonl` and asserts the canary value never appears,
    because only key names are ever read.
- **Error handling.**
  - **Typed core errors:** `RunNotFoundError`, `ArtifactAccessError` (with a code),
    `LedgerCursorError` and `RunViewError`. They carry safe context (run id, entry id, code), never
    file content.
  - **Fails per item, never per page:** every artifact is an `ArtifactSlot`, so missing, corrupt,
    unsupported, too large and denied each render their own state and recovery. A corrupt manifest
    still yields a view.
  - **Route-level errors:** only an unknown run (not found, with a Ledger link) and a lost host
    connection (FEAT-065 "Disconnected" state) are route-level.
  - **RPC mapping:** RPC errors map to JSON-RPC codes under FEAT-065's convention.
  - **No silent swallowing:** errors are never swallowed silently (memory → Coding Standards). Each
    skipped line or slot is either counted in the response (`truncated_bytes`, `partial_tail`,
    `scan_truncated`) or rendered.
- **Logging** (Pino, plan §11).
  - **Debug:**
    - per read, `{runId, read, slots states, durationMs}`;
    - JSONL index builds, `{entry_id, lines, durationMs}`.
  - **Warn:** the first corrupt artifact per (run, file) per host lifetime, as `{runId, entry_id,
state}`.
  - **Security rejections:** counted with the `ArtifactAccessError` code (FEAT-065 host log).
  - **Never logged:** file contents, excerpts, signed URLs, capabilities or tokens.
- **Accessibility** (plan §9 and §10, I9).
  - Every interactive element is a Drshya React Aria primitive.
  - Citation chips are buttons with accessible names. The evidence pane is a labelled region.
  - Focus moves only on user action and returns on close.
  - Ledger updates use a polite live region.
  - Outcome and status are conveyed by text and icon, never color alone.
  - `axe-core` runs on every route and gallery state.
- **Parity** (memory → General). Words are rendered verbatim from protocol values. `list`, `audit`
  and `report` reads return those commands' `--json` schemas (extended only by cursors and
  windows). `open` maps to the Run result route through its adapter. The FEAT-070 parity test can
  enumerate `RUN_ARTIFACT_REGISTRY`.
- **Enhancement tracking** (appended to `.spec-lite/TODO.md` under "Yantra app (plan_ui.md) —
  Phase 2 and findings"):
  1. `yantra list` flags matching the Ledger filters (outcome, mode, date range, text) and cursor
     paging, for CLI ↔ app parity.
  2. Persist claim-level quote spans so that `[n]` opens the exact supporting passage instead of
     the source excerpt.
